facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of hip pain following low-impact falls
stress fractures of the left rib, left sacrum, and left femoral neck
elevated alkaline phosphatase level of 220 U/L
phosphorus level of 2.1 mg/dL
25-OH vitamin D 14.8 ng/mL
FGF23 1241 RU/mL
Bone densitometry showed Z-scores of −2.5 in the lumbar spine and −1.9 in the femoral neck
a slow gait with a limp and lumbar tenderness
alkaline phosphatase 204 U/L
phosphorus 1.6 mg/dL
a 9×8-mm intracortical lesion in the anterolateral right fibular head

concepts.why: The patient's history of stress fractures, low phosphorus levels, and elevated FGF23 levels are consistent with X-linked hypophosphatemia.
The patient's history of stress fractures, elevated alkaline phosphatase levels, and low phosphorus levels are consistent with osteomalacia.
The patient's history of stress fractures and the presence of an intracortical lesion in the right fibular head are consistent with fibrous dysplasia.
The patient's history of stress fractures, low phosphorus levels, and elevated FGF23 levels are consistent with hypophosphatemic rickets.
The patient's history of stress fractures and the presence of an intracortical lesion in the right fibular head are consistent with McCune-Albright syndrome.
It explains the low bone density and history of stress fractures.

rationales.F02: Stress fractures are common in hypophosphatemic disorders and fibrous dysplasia.
rationales.F04: Low phosphorus levels are characteristic of hypophosphatemic disorders.
rationales.F06: Low 1,25[OH]2D3 levels are characteristic of hypophosphatemic disorders.
rationales.F07: Elevated FGF23 levels are characteristic of X-linked hypophosphatemia and other hypophosphatemic disorders.
rationales.F08: Low bone density is common in hypophosphatemic disorders and fibrous dysplasia.
rationales.F12: Intracortical lesions are characteristic of fibrous dysplasia and McCune-Albright syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: Elevated alkaline phosphatase level, low phosphorus level, and low 25-OH vitamin D level support osteomalacia, while hypophosphatemic rickets is also a strong candidate due to similar laboratory findings, but osteomalacia better explains the patient's bone pain and stress fractures without an unexplained strong contradiction.
